subject: railgunCarrier
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: six-wheeled railgun carrier braced on stabiliser legs.
Style: low-poly sci-fi military.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TypeScript module for a six-wheeled railgun carrier with deployed outrigger legs, aiming for a detailed but efficient static model built from helper functions generating around 150 parts.

I'm working out dimensions for chassis, wheels, and stabilizer legs, then designing the turret-mounted railgun assembly with rails, coils, and muzzle brake using local-to-world transform helpers for placement and elevation.

Now I'm planning the color palette (olive drab, dark gray, tan, hazard orange, cyan glow for rail energy) and building out the hull geometry with a sloped glacis profile using an extruded outline.

Still shaping hull geometry...

Next I'm adding the front cab as a box with a slanted windshield insert, then planning fender arches above each wheel on both sides.

For the wheels, I'm positioning dark tire cylinders rotated to align along the x-axis, with lighter hub caps and a ring of small bolt details on each.

For stabilizer legs, I'm planning four outriggers positioned at different z offsets on each side of the hull, with horizontal beams extending outward into angled hydraulic struts that connect down to ground pads.

For the pads, I'm sizing them as flat cylinders slightly sunk into the floor, checking proportions against overall model height. For wheels, I'm deciding whether to let them sit flush with the ground or raise them slightly for a braced look, settling on keeping the pads as the main touch points while considering whether wheels should float just above the floor instead.

Now I'm working out the hull geometry and suspension structure: adjusting wheel center height, recalculating hull bottom and outline bounds, placing the fender, and laying out the strut, beam, and cross-brace rods connecting the hull to the pads along with the hydraulic rod positions.

I'm noting that rods can be built flat-ended without joints since static models don't require bone rigging, then moving on to the turret - placing the ring and turret body boxes, defining the pivot point, and setting up the railgun barrel's forward extent from the hull front.

Now I'm checking the barrel geometry at 10° elevation: calculating the tip height and forward reach from the pivot so the barrel clears the cab roof and lands at a reasonable total length and max height around 4.3m.

Laying out the gun's internal parts next: a dark gray breech box, twin steel rail beams running the barrel's length, spacer insulators between them, a glowing cyan core strip fitted between the rails, and capacitor coil rings along the assembly.

I'm now designing collar segments that wrap around the rails as four-part open frames (top, bottom, two sides) so the rails stay visible through the gaps, repeated six times with a small cyan glow rim on each, followed by a muzzle block at the barrel's end.

Next I'm adding side cradle arms as boxes with x-axis trunnion cylinders for the pivot, capacitor bank cylinders mounted along the breech sides with cyan bands, and rod-like ammo/cable details, then laying out an octagonal turret base cylinder with trunnion tower boxes positioned to meet the gun's pivot height.

Now I'm placing a ring cylinder atop the hull for the turret deck, defining the trunnion towers as boxes straddling the gun pivot point at (0, 3.0, -1.2), sizing the breech width to fit between the towers, and adding the trunnion cylinders themselves.

For the rear, I'm designing a power plant assembly with an engine deck box, exhaust vent stacks as cylinders, and a series of thin radiator grill boxes.

I'm checking that the turret's footprint doesn't overlap the engine deck by adjusting the deck's length and center position, then starting to work out the front cab geometry, figuring out where it sits on the hull's sloped glacis and settling on placing it closer to a flatter part of the top deck instead.

I'm now placing the cab box with its flat-topped position and dimensions, checking the barrel clearance as it rotates over the cab, and designing a slanted windshield as a thin dark teal glass panel tilted backward on the cab's front face.

Moving on, I'm adding smaller details: side windows, roof sensors, antenna rods, glowing white headlight pairs, a front bumper, tow hooks, and armor skirts. I'm also sketching camo-style tan patches, orange hazard stripes on the legs, and a white number plate marking, plus storage/tool boxes mounted on the hull sides between the wheels.

Working out wheel and fender placement along the z-axis...

With hull width 2.4 I'm placing the sides at x ±1.2, then adding axle rods and diagonal suspension arms connecting the wheel centers to the hull. Now I'm setting up builder helper functions for boxes and cylinders, plus a gun elevation quaternion for the rotating part.

I'm defining gp() to transform local gun coordinates into world space via the elevation quaternion, with gbox and gcyl helpers that build rotated cylinder geometry for different axes and attach everything with flat shading and an optional glow effect, then starting to pick out olive and secondary hull colors.

I'm sketching the hull's extruded outline shape along the z-y plane, laying out the chamfered bottom and top points and checking the polygon doesn't self-intersect.

Now I'm adding the tan camo patches and side panel details as thin boxes positioned symmetrically on both sides of the hull, along with storage pods near the leg beam.

Then I'm designing the fenders over each wheel with a main panel and outer lip, checking they clear the hull and properly cover the wheel's top, followed by building the tire as a cylinder with tread blocks arranged in a ring.

Adding wheel details...

I also want a sensor mast with a radar dish on the turret, mounted near the engine deck. For each leg, I'm detailing the beam, brace, strut, piston, foot pad with ribs, hazard stripe accents, and hydraulic joint cylinders, working out the exact rod endpoints for the strut and piston geometry.

For the gun, I'm adding a small targeting sensor box with a glow lens near the breech, plus dark cable-bundle rods along the rail sides, an ammo crate with stacked projectile cylinders behind the breech, and a feeder tray. I'm also planning rear antennas, tail lights, a tow hitch, spare part, and exhaust before writing the full code.

Now I'm working out precise local coordinates for the breech, rails, and glow strip so everything fits without overlapping, and I'm laying out repeated collar brackets with top, bottom, and side plates along the rail length.

Still placing geometry blocks...

Still placing details...
